name: get_cell_ranges
description: Read cells of one worksheet: values, formulas, notes and, unless includeStyles is false, formatting. Reads several ranges in one call. Returns worksheet.cells keyed by A1 address: a plain value; [value, "=formula"] for a formula; [value, "=formula" or "", note] for a cell with a note. Empty cells are left out. styles and borders map A1 ranges to the formatting they share. At most cellLimit non-empty cells are returned, cut at a row boundary; then hasMore is true and nextRanges lists what is left. mergedRanges lists the merged areas inside the ranges: only an area's top-left cell holds its value, so check them before writing into or copying over that area.

sheetName.description: Worksheet tab name exactly as the workbook shows it, e.g. 'Sheet1' or 'Sales Data'.

cellLimit.description: The most non-empty cells to return.

name: get_range_as_csv
description: Read one range's values as CSV, without formulas or formatting: the cheapest way to read a block of data for analysis. Returns csv, rowCount (data rows, the header row not counted), columnCount, sheetName and hasMore, which is true when maxRows cut the range; read the rest with a range starting below the last row returned. Use get_cell_ranges when formulas, notes or formats matter.

sheetName.description: Worksheet tab name exactly as the workbook shows it, e.g. 'Sheet1' or 'Sales Data'.

includeHeaders.description: Whether the range's first row is a header row.

name: set_cell_range
description: Write values, formulas, notes and formatting to cells of one worksheet, given as a map from A1 address to cell; no range or size to work out. Use formula for every number derived from other cells so the workbook stays live and auditable; value is for raw inputs only. By default the call fails when a target cell holds a value or formula; set allow_overwrite only when the user asked to replace that content or agreed to it. To fill a pattern over many cells, write the pattern here and then call copy_paste_range. Formulas linking to a workbook on another computer or to a web address are refused. Returns formula_results, the computed value or error of each written formula: check it for errors such as #VALUE!, #REF! or #NAME? before you call the write done. Number formats and other formatting still need a read-back with get_cell_ranges.

sheetName.description: Worksheet tab name exactly as the workbook shows it, e.g. 'Sheet1' or 'Sales Data'.

value.description: A raw input: a label, a header or source data. Never a number you calculated: write that as a formula on its source cells.

formula.description: A formula starting with '=', e.g. '=SUM(B2:B10)' or '=B1*Assumptions!$B$3'. Use it for every value derived from other cells.

note.description: A note on the cell. Cite sources here: one note on the top-left header cell of a table taken from a file or query, or on the value cell for a figure from a web page.

numberFormat.description: Number format code, e.g. '@' for text, '0.00', '#,##0;(#,##0)' or 'yyyy-mm-dd'.

cellStyles.description: Font, fill, alignment and number format of the cell.

all.description: All four edges and the inside lines.

borderStyles.description: Borders of the cell, by edge.

value.description: Size in points; only with type points.

resizeWidth.description: Column width to set afterwards on every column the cells span.

value.description: Size in points; only with type points.

resizeHeight.description: Row height to set afterwards on every row the cells span.

name: copy_paste_range
description: Copy a range to another place on the same or another sheet. Excel adjusts relative references and repeats the pattern when the destination is larger than the source, so this is how to fill a formula down or across. copyType: all (values, formulas and formats), formats (format painter: destination values stay), values (computed values only, freezing formulas) or formulas (without formats). Fails when the destination holds values or formulas, unless copyType is formats or allow_overwrite is set after the user agreed. Fails and names the merged areas when the destination cuts across part of one: unmerge, change the destination or ask the user; do not repeat the same call. After a copy to another sheet, relative references to cells outside the copied block point at the destination sheet; copy values instead or fix the references. Returns copied, the sheet-qualified source and destination; the destination is not read back.

sourceSheetName.description: Sheet of the source range; the active sheet when left out.

destSheetName.description: Sheet to paste into; sourceSheetName when left out.

destRange.description: A1 notation, e.g. 'A1:C10', 'B5', 'D:D' or '5:5'. May be larger than the source to repeat it.

name: execute_office_js
description: Run Office.js code in the open workbook for what the other tools do not cover: changing the format of existing ranges, clearing, inserting or deleting rows and columns, sheets, Excel tables, charts, pivot tables, conditional formatting, sorting and filtering, data validation, grouping, freezing panes and named ranges. The task pane runs the code inside Excel.run on its main thread, with nothing else in scope: no network (fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket), no dialogs, no add-in or file APIs. Calls that reach the network, links that make Excel open another computer's workbook, and changes to settings outside this workbook are refused before they run; tell the user what was refused instead of trying another way. Each call may need the user's approval under their permission settings; the card shows the explanation and the code. Returns success and the code's return value.

code.description: Body of an async function with context (the Excel.RequestContext) and the Excel enums in scope: write the statements directly, without wrapping them in another function, which would never be called. load what you read and await context.sync() before using it. Sync every write before the code returns: writes still queued when it returns are reported as an error and do not happen. return a JSON-serializable value; it becomes the result, cut to the result budget. attachImage(base64Png) adds an image to the result for you to look at. Each context.sync() may take at most 30 seconds and the whole call 90 seconds; after a timeout the code may still finish in the background, so read back before you retry.

explanation.description: What the code does, in at most 50 characters; shown on the approval card.

name: read_surface_context
description: The workbook's state for this turn: the active sheet, the selected range or ranges (several separated by ' | ') and any selected chart; on the first turn also <initial_state> (each sheet's name and size, and its Excel tables with their columns), and <user_changes> with what the user changed outside this chat since your last turn, renames included. This call and its result are added at the start of each turn, so you rarely need it; calling it yourself returns only the current sheet, selection and chart.
